steps: Entered seed T2026-RUS-DAN01 via Play a seed
Played months 1-12 of One Term as Russia (desk months 1-8, map months 3, 9-12)
Used All orders, forecasts, Ask your staff, Why your score moved
Final month: struck Turkey's nuclear facilities as an edge case
scenarios.notes: Learned the limits well: political capital cap and loss, meeting limit of 3, diminishing returns on National address (named in the report). Did not play to the end of the term, and I still do not know if the 115 score mission is reachable (score drifts 100 to 90, 'heading to 86').

steps: Repeated National address two months running (+4 then +2.4, 'smaller each time')
Tried ceasefire proposals (6% then 9%, both failed)
Struck Turkey nuclear facilities: approval +4, stability +4, tension +12, Erdogan keeps the door ajar
scenarios.notes: Repeat-spam is correctly discouraged. The Turkey strike looked like a free win, which is the dominant-move smell I hate.

friction.expected: A code field next to the button
friction.happened: Seed box appears only after pressing Play a seed; worked first time, seed accepted

Mojtaba Khamenei as Supreme Leader, Prime Minister Andy Burnham (UK), Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi (Japan), Kramatorsk fortress belt: newest office holders I would not know; I chose I know this, so no underline helped; the who-is-who strip on the first screen did help for Khamenei only

friction.where: Month 10 call, Terror in the capital
friction.happened: 'the network' behind the terror in Poland (answer: Strike the network's sponsors) is never named; foreign interference events do not say which agency
Button flips to Hide sizes but crisis answers stay worded as 'down a lot'; only orders get numbers (forecast)
Opened the full report tab instead; the explanation was in a different tab
Cost shown as coin icons; numbers only appear in the right panel after adding; orders marked free still cost a defense budget percent
Early months the one suggestion was Offer defense pact to China, disabled ('won't sign in the middle of a war'). A suggestion that can never be used
Label says what orders cost but the number is what is left after my planned spending (month 9: header 2 of 6, right panel 3 now); it changes as I click
Capital hit the cap of 6 and 1-2 per month was lost; nothing in the default flow pushes you to spend it

friction.expected: Advice that varies with the situation
friction.happened: 'Reassure: no threat intended' recommended for nearly every Western call, month after month

friction.expected: My ceasefire proposal as the headline
friction.happened: The only thing I chose myself (failed ceasefire, 6%) sat in a small 'also this month' tile under a staff meeting headline

friction.where: Orders search with no field focused
friction.happened: Typing 'ceasefire ukraine' with no field focused fired hotkeys (M switched Map to Desk)
Choice explained -3; the other -7 has no line under Why your numbers moved (only counter-intelligence, war weariness, economy)

friction.expected: To find and close the open call
friction.happened: Stayed at 1 open from month 7 to 13 and I could not see which call it was; the assassination-attempt crisis from month 3 reappeared in month 13
Identical card to month 3 (same quote, same three answers); the quote 'I did not vote for them, but this was the right call' is used for different choices
Approval +4, stability +4; Erdogan 'takes the call and keeps the door ajar', Trump 'I will put it to my government'
Dropdown clipped, only Cabinet and World visible
Score fell 100 to 90 over a year and 'heading to 86' while the mission needs 115; no way to see the lever
Left card covers part of the globe and the globe auto-rotates to each card; fine, but Europe is often under the card
Nuclear strike on Ukraine card shows 'free' beside NO UNDO; free refers to capital only

suggestions.goal_served: Can find out why every number moved

suggestions.what: List every contributor to a big stability or approval move in the report, with sizes, and link Why? to the same card

Meeting limit with 'Your calendar is full' (043-pre6.png)

fun.reason: Real trade-offs in the orders (capital, meeting slots, forecasts) but the routine cabinet flow made most months click-through

clarity.reason: Staff advice is clear about who recommends what; the capital number and open-call counter muddy it

visual.reason: Handsome scenes and a readable map at 1920x1080

feels_like_a_game.reason: Report cards and deadlines feel like a game; the recycled quotes and calls do not

agency.reason: Only blocked by a disabled suggestion; I always saw why

realism.reason: Debt 2000%, Turkey strike reward, near-identical foreign calls month after month

replay.reason: Want to try other seats, but doubt a Term has 48 months of fresh decisions

recommend.reason: Good transparency for a strategy fan; depth over time still unproven

verbatim: The numbers are honest, which most games are not. But when the same call from Kim comes back with the same words and the Foreign Minister says reassure again, I start to wonder if there is a game under it.
